The strict read-replica guard now verifies that the replica's snapshot has caught up to the revision being read (snapshot domination) instead of checking a single transaction id, and raises from within the read itself rather than from a trailing assertion, so a replica that catches up mid-query can no longer let an incomplete read through. - This release mostly addresses Wasmtime security advisories.
- Open multi-DB SQLite connections with in-memory "main".
- Apply base+user migrations on non-default "main" SQLite databases.
- Internal: share refinery implementations across `rusqlite` and `trailbase_sqlite`.
- Update Dependencies.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/trailbaseio/trailbase/compare/v0.35.7...v0.35.8

- Enable HTTP2 negotiation to allow Browsers to multiplex more SSE streams.
- Untangle WASM SQLite extension function runtime from WASM HTTP handlers and tidy up implementation. Properly wire binary version to SQLite function initialization.
- Refine shutdown order: drop more sooner.
- Update dependencies.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/trailbaseio/trailbase/compare/v0.35.6...v0.35.7

- Add explicit DB shutdown order to avoid an issues w/o implicit destruction even though it was working just fine.
- Avoid truncating SQLite WALs on implicit connection closure. In multi-DBs setups, we don't want to interfere with other connections when a cached connection is evicted.

- Fix DB connection destruction order issue that prevented SQLite from cleaning up auxiliary files.
- Update Rust and JavaScript dependencies. Address `zstd-safe`'s security advisories.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/trailbaseio/trailbase/compare/v0.35.4...v0.35.5

- Explicitly truncate SQLite WALs on shutdown.
- Bound the number of password hashing threads.
- Fix building the CLI w/o the default WASM feature.
- Update dependencies. Addresses securiy advisories and bumps SQLite to v3.54.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/trailbaseio/trailbase/compare/v0.35.3...v0.35.4

- Make refresh tokens optional allowing to run off sessions entirely in favor of purely stateless tokens.
- When RecordApi RLA queries fail, log the error to `stderr` to avoid silently failing malformed queries.
- Update dependencies. Addresses Tokio security advisories.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/trailbaseio/trailbase/compare/v0.35.2...v0.35.3

- Fix graceful DB shutdown for busy backlogs and extend wait time to allow logs to be written safely. This came to light as a result of increased throughput.
- Tidy up `User` and `DbUser` memory representations resulting in ~5% throughput increases. As we keep pushing, even small optimizations start to matter.

- Major post-v0.35 clean-up: simpler ownership, less reference counting and more consistent flows across acrions.
- Update dependencies.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/trailbaseio/trailbase/compare/v0.35.0...v0.35.1

- Fewer yields and thus less congestion during record handling.
  - Doubles the insert throughput and results in roughly 10% faster reads.
- Enable file writes as part of transactions and batch-operations.
- Batch insertions now return a fake "skipped" id, when an insertion conflict was ignored based on the API's policy.
  - This is more in line with the transaction endpoint's behavior but technically a breaking change. This will only matter to you if you're using batch insertions, with an ignore policy
